profile.summary: PhyloGPN is a convolutional network that reads DNA sequence alone and outputs, for every position, the parameters of a nucleotide substitution model (Felsenstein's F81). It was trained to fit those parameters to columns of the Zoonomia multispecies whole-genome alignment given a phylogenetic tree, which makes the output a statement about how constrained each site is. It needs no alignment at prediction time, so it can score variants and supply embeddings from a single sequence.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/models/phylogpn.md opening paragraph; model card first paragraph; arXiv abstract

summary_quotes.text: PhyloGPN learns position-specific parameters of the Felsenstein F81 substitution model from a phylogenetic alignment. Inference needs only DNA sequence, which makes the published model useful for transfer learning and zero-shot variant scoring away from a reference genome.
PhyloGPN is a convolutional neural network that takes encoded DNA sequences as input and outputs rate matrix parameters for
Our approach integrates an alignment into the loss function during training but does not require it for making predictions, thereby enhancing the model's applicability.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The network is convolutional: 20 stacks of 2 layers with kernel size 5, inner dimension 480 and outer dimension 960, and a receptive field of 481 positions. It is trained to maximise the likelihood of each alignment column under a phylogenetic tree: the output at a position gives the F81 rate parameters for that site, and the stationary distribution of that substitution process says how viable each allele is there. Because the tree and alignment enter only through the loss, prediction takes plain sequence. The model works as a sliding window: an input of length l yields outputs for the l minus 480 central positions, so sequences are padded before scoring.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is published, songlab/PhyloGPN, read here at revision a763739c. It is one of four model families in the songlab-cal/gpn package, which supports PhyloGPN for inference only, not training or fine-tuning, and reaches it through AutoClass APIs rather than the gpn command line. The checkpoint ships its own modelling code, so loading needs trust_remote_code. A result should name the checkpoint revision, the padding used and the window conventions.

run_guide.summary: Install the gpn package, load the published PhyloGPN checkpoint and get embeddings and log rate parameters for a batch of short sequences.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The installation page states GPN supports Python 3.13.
PyTorch; the installation page says accelerator selection depends on your platform and points to the official PyTorch installer for CUDA.
Loading the checkpoint runs code from its Hugging Face repository (trust_remote_code=True).
No alignment and no reference genome are needed for inference.

steps.title: Load the checkpoint through the package
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModel

register_auto_classes("phylo")

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("songlab/PhyloGPN")
print(model.config)
PY
steps.explanation: The documentation's quick start, wrapped in a heredoc, with a print of the configuration added to confirm the load. This is one of two loading routes: the package registers the AutoClasses for you. Note that pip install gpn is not pinned to the commit read for this page.

steps.title: Score a batch of sequences
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

checkpoint = "songlab/PhyloGPN"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(checkpoint, trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(checkpoint, trust_remote_code=True)

# Example data
seqs = [
    "TATAAA",
    "GGCCAATCT",
    "CACGTG",
    "AGGTCACGT",
    "GCCAGCC",
    "GGGGATTTCC"
]

# Output length is input length minus 480 (the receptive field size minus 1)
pad_token = tokenizer.pad_token
pad_size = 481 // 2
pad_sequence = lambda seq: pad_token * pad_size + seq + pad_token * pad_size
padded_seqs = [pad_sequence(seq) for seq in seqs]
input_tensor = tokenizer(padded_seqs, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)["input_ids"]

with torch.no_grad():
    padded_embeddings = model.get_embeddings(input_tensor)
    padded_logits = model(input_tensor) # These are log rate parameters for the F81 model

embeddings = []
logits = []

for i in range(len(seqs)):
    length = len(seqs[i])
    embeddings.append(padded_embeddings[i, :length])
    logits.append({})

    for k in "ACGT":
        logits[-1][k] = padded_logits[k][i, :length]

print(embeddings[0].shape, {k: v.shape for k, v in logits[0].items()})
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's example, wrapped in a heredoc, with a print of the first sequence's embedding and logit shapes added. It pads each sequence so that outputs cover every input position. This is the second loading route: it skips the gpn package and loads the checkpoint's own code with trust_remote_code, so it can be run instead of the previous step.
